items.headline: Valkyries are champions — Golden State wins the first-ever Finals Game 7
items.body: In only their second season, the Golden State Valkyries beat the Atlanta Dream 68-63 in the first winner-take-all Game 7 in WNBA Finals history. Gabby Williams poured in 30 and took Finals MVP, and Veronica Burton iced it from the line with 5.1 seconds left.
items.say: A brand-new expansion team just won it all in a Game 7 — did you catch how tense that finish was?

items.headline: Canelo is back — he decisions unbeaten Mbilli to reclaim the WBC belt
items.body: Thirteen months after losing to Terence Crawford, Saúl 'Canelo' Álvarez returned in Riyadh and won a clear unanimous decision over previously unbeaten Christian Mbilli (115-112, 116-111, 117-110) to grab back the WBC super middleweight title.
items.say: Canelo bounced right back from that Crawford loss and handed an undefeated guy his first L — think he's still got it?

items.headline: Wemby is a problem — 43 points and six blocks as the Spurs roll
items.body: Victor Wembanyama went supernova on Halloween night, dropping 43 points with six blocks and seven boards in a 121-111 Spurs win over Minnesota — San Antonio's fourth straight to open the season.
items.say: Wembanyama just put up 43 and SIX blocks in one game — is anyone going to be able to stop this guy this year?

items.headline: Chelsea put two past Manchester United at the Bridge
items.body: Chelsea handled Manchester United 2-0 at Stamford Bridge in Saturday's big one, turning up the heat on United early and never letting go. A tidy weekend for the Blues in the title race.
items.say: Chelsea beat United 2-0 this weekend — you still keeping an eye on the Premier League at all?

items.headline: USC stuns No. 2 Ohio State 30-18 under the Coliseum lights
items.body: Lincoln Riley's USC pulled off the upset of the weekend, knocking off second-ranked Ohio State 30-18 behind freshman QB Jayden Maiava. It's the Buckeyes' second loss already — their earliest two-loss start since 2011.
items.say: USC just took down No. 2 Ohio State with a freshman quarterback — college football is wild this year, huh?

items.headline: FURIA complete an insane comeback to win PGL Bucharest
items.body: Down 2-13 on the opening map, Brazil's FURIA stormed all the way back to beat Nemiga 3-2 and take the $450K PGL Masters Bucharest title. Veteran FalleN lifts his 48th career trophy, and YEKINDAR grabbed his first-ever MVP.
items.say: A CS team was down 2-13 on the first map and still came back to win the whole thing — how do you even recover from that?

items.headline: A $7M documentary is quietly winning the box office
items.body: Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim's strange, buzzy Elizabeth Holmes documentary 'You Can See Everything' edged superhero-horror 'Clayface' to top a slow Halloween weekend — a rare feat for a doc.
items.say: A documentary actually beat a superhero movie at the box office this weekend — have you heard about this Elizabeth Holmes one?

items.headline: 'The Gilded Age' is back — Season 4 premieres tonight
items.body: HBO's lavish, deliciously catty period drama returns Sunday night for Season 4, with the Russells' marriage under strain and Agnes van Rhijn plotting her way back to the top of society.
items.say: The Gilded Age is back tonight — are you a fan, or is costume drama not your thing?

items.headline: Jay-Z is headlining the Super Bowl halftime show
items.body: It's official: Jay-Z will headline the Super Bowl LXI halftime show on February 14, 2027, at SoFi Stadium — his first time taking the big stage himself after producing the show for years through Roc Nation.
items.say: Jay-Z is finally doing the Super Bowl halftime show himself — who are you hoping he brings out as a surprise guest?
